_comment: Success-score component weights, per position. Goal contributions (perf_level/perf_delta) are a weak-to-meaningless signal for defenders/goalkeepers (most keepers have 0 goals+assists both before and after a move), so their weight is shifted toward the FotMob-derived components instead - the ones actually built to differ by position (see compute_fotmob_component_pcts in build_dataset.py - FotMob's own per-match rating; goals/xG/xA/dribbles/chances-created for attacking; tackles/interceptions/clearances/recoveries for outfielders or saves/save%/goals-conceded for goalkeepers under defensive; accurate passes/90 for possession), kept separate rather than blended into one number so a player's actual profile (e.g. an attack-minded fullback vs. a purely defensive one) survives into the score. Each is only known for the subset of transfers with FotMob tenure stats for that specific bucket (data/raw/fotmob_stats_cache.csv, built by scripts/fetch_fotmob_stats.py - optional, like the resale/loan cache below) - for a row missing a bucket, that bucket's weight is dropped and the other weights renormalized, same pattern as resale_profit, independently per bucket. value_growth, value_for_money, AND rating are all deliberately FLAT across every position (0.15/0.10/0.20) - value_growth/value_for_money because they're each a single global percentile rank with no position grouping at all (unlike perf_level/defensive/etc., which are ranked within position), so there was never a real football-role reason for their weight to vary by position; rating because it's the same metric (FotMob's own overall per-match quality score) regardless of role, unlike attacking/defensive/possession which are literally different stats depending on position. value_for_money was originally flat at 0.20 (moved there from a 0.20/0.22/0.22/0.25 position-by-position spread that was really just leftover perf_level weight, not a deliberate choice) but that's still a lot of weight on one fee-vs-performance metric, so it's now 0.10 - the freed 0.10 is routed into attacking/defensive/possession (scaled proportionally per position, same mechanism as the original flattening), NOT into rating, which is funded separately (see below). value_for_money's own performance side (see value_for_money_performance_proxy in build_dataset.py) is perf_level_pct for every position except Goalkeeper, where it's defensive_pct instead - perf_level_pct (goal contributions) is meaningless for goalkeepers (82% have exactly 0, all tied at the same percentile regardless of quality), which silently degraded value_for_money into 'was the fee reasonable' alone for most keepers, with no real performance signal at all. rating went from a 2-8% position-by-position spread to a flat 0.10, then up again to a flat 0.20 - a per-match rating from an outside service reflects a lot more than the handful of counting stats every other component is built from (positioning, decision-making, composure - things a stat line alone misses), so it earned a real seat at the table rather than a token one. Both moves were funded entirely from perf_level/perf_delta/playing_time (scaled down proportionally, preserving their relative ratio to each other) rather than from value_growth/value_for_money (kept flat in their own right) or attacking/defensive/possession (reserved for role-specific tuning - see _sub_positions_comment). Some positions (Centre-Back/full-back especially, whose perf_level/perf_delta/playing_time bloc was already small) end up with a very thin sliver left for perf_level/perf_delta/playing_time individually as a result - that's an accepted tradeoff of funding rating from a shrinking pool without touching the role-specific buckets. Goalkeeper's playing_time is the one exception to that erosion: it used to sit at 0.17, deliberately the highest of any position - a club fields exactly one starting keeper, so whether they nail down the #1 spot is an unusually clean, binary signal, unlike an outfield rotation slot - but both rating bumps (perf_level/perf_delta already being 0 for goalkeepers) drained it down to 0.05, only partially recovered by a later flat +5% edit. Restored to 0.17 here, funded from defensive (0.35 -> 0.28, which still remains by far Goalkeeper's largest weight) rather than from the flat components, so the one-starting-XI-slot reasoning isn't silently lost to unrelated funding mechanics again. resale_profit's weight is NOT the flat number below - it varies by tenure length per resale_weight_curve (a quick flip weights resale heavily since that's often the point of the deal; a long career barely moves regardless of the eventual sale price, since the club already extracted years of value). The number here is just the weight at the curve's ~2-year reference point, kept for documentation. Only known for the ~17% of transfers where the club actually resold the player for a recorded fee - for the rest it's excluded and the other weights are renormalized to sum to 1 (see build_dataset.py). Shared by scripts/build_dataset.py (computes the label) and app/main.py (labels the 'why this score' explanation). Each position row (including resale_profit) must sum to 1.0. rating was raised from a flat 0.20 to 0.30 for the four outfield defensive sub-positions (Defensive Midfield, Centre-Back, Left-Back, Right-Back) and the broad Defender fallback, funded entirely from defensive (0.23/0.29/0.26/0.26/0.23 down to 0.13/0.19/0.16/0.16/0.13) - checked directly against the real dataset: rating correlates with success_score far more strongly than the defensive bucket does for every one of these positions (0.84-0.86 vs. 0.50-0.58), a gap not seen for attacking positions (attacking correlates as well as or better than rating there, 0.79-0.91) or goalkeepers (saves/goals-conceded correlates nearly as well as rating, 0.73 vs. 0.80) - so this is specifically an outfield-defender pattern, not a general "rating is undervalued" one. Motivated by Declan Rice, Rodri, and other elite ball-playing defensive midfielders/centre-backs whose FotMob rating is consistently far ahead of their raw tackle/interception/clearance percentile - raw defensive-action counting rewards a high-volume destroyer style and says little about the positioning and game intelligence that keep a genuinely elite defender from needing to make those actions in the first place, which a holistic per-match rating captures far better.
_sub_positions_comment: Sub-position weight overrides (see build_dataset.py's lookup_weights and SUB_POSITION_WEIGHTS) - a player's actual career-wide fielded sub-position (from game_lineups.csv, not the single undated label in players.csv - see load_actual_sub_positions) selects one of these rows INSTEAD of the broad position row above, when one exists for it; percentile ranking itself still groups by the broad position above, only the weights differ - a Centre-Back is still ranked against all Defenders, just weighted differently once ranked. Only sub-positions with a real, well-established difference in role expectations get an explicit row here (Defensive Midfield vs. Attacking Midfield vs. wide midfield; Centre-Back vs. full-back; winger); Central Midfield, Centre-Forward, Second Striker, and Goalkeeper fall back to their broad position's row unchanged - either because that IS the broad default's implicit profile (Central Midfield, Centre-Forward), the position has no sub-split at all (Goalkeeper), or the sample is too thin in this dataset for a confident, distinct opinion (Second Striker, ~300 players total before any transfer/appearance filters). Each row still needs perf_level/perf_delta/value_growth/playing_time/value_for_money/rating/attacking/defensive/possession/resale_profit and must sum to 1.0, same as the broad rows. The directional idea throughout: dial perf_level+perf_delta+attacking (the same 'attacking output' bloc fold_perf_level_into_attacking folds into one number) down for a defense-oriented sub-position and up for an attack-oriented one, moving that weight into defensive/possession instead - the FotMob buckets that actually differ by role. Attacking Midfield's possession in particular is set explicitly (0.13, alongside Winger/Defensive Midfield) rather than purely mechanically - a naive proportional scaling during an earlier weight change had compressed it to 0.03, far below every comparable sub-position, which made no football sense for a possession-heavy #10 role. Full-back's defensive is likewise set explicitly to 0.26 (funded from perf_level/perf_delta/attacking) rather than left at the smaller mechanically-derived value - a full-back is still fundamentally a defender, and their weight profile now sits close to Centre-Back's (defensive 0.26 vs. 0.29, attacking 0.03 vs. 0.01), just with a little more license to contribute going forward. value_growth, value_for_money, and rating are flat 0.15/0.10/0.20 here too, same as the broad rows above and for the same reason - none of the three have a football-role basis to vary at this level either. Caicedo (Chelsea, Defensive Midfield) is the motivating case - see the README section on sub-position weighting.

resale_weight_curve._comment: resale_weight(tenure_years) = min + (max - min) * exp(-tenure_years / decay_years). A few months' tenure -> ~18-20% weight; ~2 years -> ~8.6% (close to the old flat 8%); 6+ years -> under 3%.

value_for_money_weight_curve._comment: value_for_money_weight(tenure_years), same formula and reasoning as resale_weight_curve: whether the fee looked reasonable at signing time is close to the whole story for a short spell, and fades toward irrelevant for a long, clearly-successful career already fully judged by every tenure-long performance component elsewhere in the score - a long career doesn't get there by being conditioned on 'and they were good', the same way resale_profit isn't; that's already what the rest of the score measures. Decays slower than resale (3-year vs. 2-year decay_years) since 'was the fee worth it' plausibly stays a live question a little longer than 'how the eventual resale went'. A few months' tenure -> ~14% weight; ~2 years -> ~8.7%; 6 years -> ~3.8%. Replaces the flat 0.10 reference value below at runtime (see build_dataset.py) - the flat number is kept only for documentation/renormalization-when-missing purposes, same pattern as resale_profit.
